originalTitle: Two rescued after Nairobi building collapse with five still missing
title: Sad News in Nairobi: A Building Fell Down, But Helpers Are Amazing!
content:
Hello, my wonderful friends! Your kid-friendly news reporter is here with some important news from Nairobi, a very big city in our amazing Africa. Sometimes, sad things happen, and it's good to talk about them simply. We heard some news about a big building that had a problem.

What Happened in Nairobi?

Imagine a really tall building. A building is like a giant house where many people can live or work. In Nairobi, a big city in Kenya, there was a building that was still being built. It wasn't finished yet. But something very sad happened. This big building fell down. Poof! It just collapsed. It's like when you build a tall tower with your blocks, and sometimes it just tumbles down. But this was a real, big building. This happened very suddenly. When a building falls down, it can be very scary. People got worried, and everyone wanted to help. Did you know? Buildings are made to be very, very strong! They have deep foundations, like super strong feet, that go into the ground to hold them up. Architects are special people who draw plans for buildings to make sure they are safe.

Heroes to the Rescue!

When the building fell, many wonderful heroes came running! These were the rescue teams. They are super brave men and women who help people in danger. The police were there, and firefighters, and doctors, and even regular people from the community. Everyone worked together like a big team. They used special tools to try and find people who might have been inside. They listened very carefully for any sounds. They dug through the fallen pieces of the building. It was very hard work, but they didn't give up. They wanted to help everyone. Did you know? Rescue teams sometimes use special dogs called search and rescue dogs! These clever dogs have super noses that can sniff out people even under lots of rubble. They are truly hero dogs!

Two Friends Found, Some Are Still Missing

The good news is that the brave helpers found two people! They were stuck, but the rescuers helped them get out safely. Isn't that wonderful? We are so happy for them and their families. But the helpers are still working very hard. There are still five people who have not been found yet. This means the rescue teams are still searching with all their might. It makes us feel a bit sad to think about them, but we hope very, very much that they will be found soon too. It's like when you play hide-and-seek, but in a very serious way. The helpers won't stop looking until they have searched everywhere. Our hearts are with the families waiting for their loved ones.

Why Did the Building Fall Down?

This is a very important question. Buildings should not just fall down. When people build something big, they have to follow very strict rules. These rules are like a recipe for making a super strong cake! They say how much cement to use, how many strong bars to put inside, and how to make sure everything is safe. Sometimes, grown-ups called the 'owner' of the building and the 'contractor' (who is like the main builder) might not follow all these important rules. Maybe they tried to build too fast, or they didn't use strong enough materials, or they didn't check everything properly. This can make a building weak, even if it looks big and strong from the outside. Did you know? Good buildings use strong materials like steel and concrete. Steel bars are put inside concrete to make it super strong, just like how bones make your body strong! The police are now looking for the building's owner and the contractor. They want to ask them questions. They want to find out why the building fell. This is not to be mean, but to make sure that this kind of sad thing doesn't happen again. They want to keep everyone safe in Nairobi and all over Africa.

Learning and Staying Safe

This sad news reminds us how important it is for buildings to be built properly. It teaches us that adults have a very big job to make sure everything around us is safe. From our homes to our schools, we rely on grown-ups to follow the rules and build things strong. Always remember that many, many people work every day to keep you safe. Your parents, your teachers, the police, and all the community helpers are always thinking about your safety. And if you ever see something that doesn't look safe, it's always good to tell a trusted adult. Did you know? In many places, building inspectors are special people who check buildings as they are being built to make sure they are following all the safety rules. They are like super safety detectives!

A Message of Hope

Even though this news is a bit sad, we can also see the good in people. We see how brave the rescuers are. We see how people in Nairobi are helping each other. When sad things happen, it's important for us to stick together and help each other. Let's send our kind thoughts to everyone in Nairobi, especially to the families who are waiting. We hope for good news soon. And let's remember that our communities are strong, and we will always work hard to make sure our homes and cities are safe and wonderful places to live. Thank you for listening, my little champions. Stay curious and stay kind!
summary: In Nairobi, Kenya, a big building that was still being built fell down, but brave rescuers found two people, and they are still looking for others while police try to understand why it collapsed.
whyMatters: This news matters because it teaches us how important it is for buildings to be built very safely so that everyone can live and work without worrying, and it shows us how people help each other when sad things happen.

originalTitle: Woman, 65, becomes second patient to die of Ebola in Kenya
title: Let's Stay Healthy and Safe in Africa! Your Kid Reporter Says Hello!
content:
Hello, hello, my super friends across beautiful Africa! It's your kid-friendly news reporter here, ready to share some very important news about staying healthy and happy. We live in such an amazing continent, full of sunshine, laughter, and incredible people. And just like we learn about playing safely and sharing our toys, it's super important to learn about keeping our bodies safe too! Sometimes, there are tiny, tiny things called germs that we can't even see. Most germs are just little nuisances, maybe giving us a sniffly nose or a small cough. But sometimes, there are special germs that can make people very, very sick. Today, we're going to talk about one of these special germs called Ebola. Don't worry, we're talking about it so we can all learn how to stay strong and healthy together!

What Are Germs, Really?

Imagine tiny, invisible creatures floating all around us! That's what germs are like. Some germs are good and help our tummies digest food. But others, the ones we worry about, can make us feel tired, hot, or even give us a tummy ache. Our bodies have super defenders, like tiny soldiers, that fight off these bad germs. But sometimes, the bad germs are very tricky. Did you know? You can't see germs with your eyes! They are smaller than a tiny speck of dust. You need a very special magnifying glass, called a microscope, to see them dancing around.

What is Ebola? A Tricky Germ

Ebola is one of those tricky germs. It's not like a normal cold that spreads when someone sneezes in the air. This special germ likes to spread through touching. It can make people very, very sick, very quickly. That's why grown-ups, doctors, and health heroes work extra hard to make sure everyone knows how to keep it from spreading. Ebola germs like to be in the body fluids of someone who is sick. What are body fluids? Things like sweat, spit, or even blood. If a sick person touches something, and then another person touches that same thing and then touches their eyes, nose, or mouth, the germ can jump. That's why we need to be super careful with our hands! Did you know? The Ebola germ is named after a river in Africa! It was first found near the Ebola River a long, long time ago.

A Story of Care in Kenya

Recently, in the wonderful country of Kenya, something important happened. We heard some sad news about a kind grandmother who became very, very sick. She was important to her family, just like your grandmothers are important to you. She got sick because she was a close family member of someone else who had also become sick after traveling. That person had traveled all the way from another African country called the Democratic Republic of Congo. This reminds us how important it is to pay attention and learn how to keep ourselves safe from tricky germs like Ebola. When someone travels from far away, sometimes germs can travel with them, even if they don't know it right away. That's why countries work together to make sure everyone is safe, especially at places where people cross borders. Did you know? Kenya is famous for its amazing wildlife, like lions, elephants, and giraffes! It's a beautiful country with very kind people.

How Can We Keep Ebola Away? Be a Super Protector!

This is the most important part, my friends! Here’s how you can be a super protector against Ebola and other tricky germs: 1. **Wash Your Hands, Hands, Hands!** This is like magic! Use soap and clean water to wash your hands often, especially before you eat, after you use the toilet, and after playing outside. Sing a happy song while you wash for at least 20 seconds. This washes all those tiny, invisible germs right down the drain! 2. **Don't Touch Sick People (and What They've Touched):** If someone is very sick, it's best to keep a little distance. And try not to touch things they might have touched, like their clothes or blankets. It's not because you don't love them, but because you want to keep everyone safe. 3. **Tell a Grown-Up:** If you or someone you know feels very, very sick (like a fever, feeling very weak, or a tummy ache), tell a grown-up right away! Your parents, teachers, or guardians know what to do and can get help quickly. Did you know? Washing your hands with soap and water is like giving germs a big, slippery slide right off your skin! It's one of the best ways to stay healthy.

Our Health Heroes: Doctors and Nurses!

We have amazing health heroes in Africa! Our doctors, nurses, and health workers are like superheroes. They are very brave and clever. When someone gets sick with Ebola, these heroes wear special clothes, like astronaut suits, to protect themselves from the germs while they help the sick person. They give medicine and special care to try and make the sick person feel better. It's very important that people who get sick with Ebola go to a special hospital right away. The health heroes there know exactly what to do to help them get well and to stop the germ from spreading to others. They are working super hard to keep our communities safe. Did you know? Health heroes wear special suits, gloves, and masks. This helps them stay safe while they are busy caring for people who are sick, making sure the germs don't jump to them.

Working Together to Stay Safe in Our Community

Just like a football team works together to score a goal, everyone in our community needs to work together to stay safe from germs. Our leaders, health workers, and even young people like you have a part to play! In Kenya, and other countries, people are working hard. They are checking people who travel to make sure they are healthy. They are teaching everyone about washing hands and staying safe. When we all listen to our grown-ups and follow these simple rules, we make our whole community stronger and safer. We don't need to be scared, but we do need to be smart and careful. Being kind to people who are sick, and supporting our health heroes, makes us all super citizens. Did you know? When everyone works together and follows safety rules, we are much stronger than any tricky germ! We can keep our families and friends safe.

A Bright Future for Africa!

So, my wonderful friends, remember to keep those hands clean, tell a grown-up if you feel sick, and always listen to your teachers and parents. By being smart and careful, we can all help make Africa a healthier, happier place for everyone to learn, play, and grow. Let's keep playing, learning, and growing strong together! We are a continent full of joy and resilience, and together, we can overcome anything. Stay safe, stay healthy, and keep shining bright! Your Kid Reporter, signing off!
summary: Your kid reporter shares important news from Kenya about staying safe from a tricky germ called Ebola, emphasizing handwashing and listening to grown-ups to keep everyone healthy.
whyMatters: This is important because knowing about germs like Ebola helps us learn how to keep ourselves, our families, and our friends safe and healthy.

originalTitle: Hospitals deliberately targeted by Sudan's RSF fighters, BBC finds
title: Hospitals are for Helping, Not Hurting! A Story from Sudan
content:
Hello, amazing kids of Africa! Your friendly news reporter, Kiki, is here with an important story from our beautiful continent. My name is Kiki the Reporter, and today we are going to talk about something happening in a country called Sudan. Sudan is a big country in Africa, just like many of your homes! Sometimes, grown-ups fight, and it can be very sad. We are going to learn about how special places called hospitals are getting hurt there. But don't worry, we will talk about how we can hope for peace and kindness too! In Sudan, some grown-ups are having a big disagreement. This means they are fighting each other. When grown-ups fight, it can be scary, and sometimes people get hurt. It's like when you and your friend might argue, but much, much bigger. When there is fighting, people need help. Where do we go when we need help if we get a boo-boo or feel sick? That's right, we go to a hospital! Hospitals are magical places where doctors and nurses work very hard to make everyone feel better. They give us medicine, put bandages on cuts, and help us be strong again. Imagine a superhero, but instead of flying, they help you feel better with a smile and some kind words! Now, let's talk about hospitals. They are super, super special!

Why Hospitals Are Super Special Places

Hospitals are places where everyone, no matter who they are or where they come from, can get help. If you have a tummy ache, or fall down and scrape your knee, a hospital is there for you. Doctors and nurses work so hard to make sure everyone is safe and healthy. They help little babies, grandmas, grandpas, moms, and dads. They are like guardian angels, always ready to lend a helping hand. **Did you know?** Hospitals are supposed to be safe places, even when there is fighting outside. This is a very old rule that grown-ups all over the world agree on! Everyone needs to be able to go to a hospital without being scared. It's like how your school is a safe place for you to learn and play, no matter what is happening outside. We all want our friends and family to be able to get help if they are sick or hurt, right? That's why hospitals are so important. Sadly, in Sudan, some people who are fighting are doing something very, very wrong. A group called the 'Rapid Support Forces' – let's just call them 'some people fighting' for now – are hurting hospitals on purpose. The BBC, which is like a big news channel that helps us know what's happening in the world, found out about this. They found that these fighters are going into hospitals, making it hard for doctors and nurses to do their job, and sometimes even damaging the buildings. Imagine if someone came to your school and made it impossible for your teachers to teach! That's how serious it is. This makes it very, very hard for sick and hurt people to get the help they need. This is not okay. When someone does something very, very bad during a fight, like hurting hospitals or people who are not fighting, we have a special name for it. It's called a 'war crime.'

What Are "War Crimes"?

A war crime is like breaking the biggest, most important rules that people should follow, even when they are in a very big argument or fight. These rules are there to protect people who can't fight back, like sick people in hospitals, or children. It's like having rules in a game – if someone cheats in a very bad way, they are breaking the rules. But these are real-life rules that help keep people safe and alive. Hurting hospitals is one of these big, big rule breaks. It makes it very hard for everyone to get better, and it makes people very scared. **Did you know?** There are special rules that countries all over the world agree on to try and make fighting less scary and dangerous for everyday people. These rules say that hospitals, doctors, and nurses must always be safe and allowed to help people. There's a very important grown-up named Mr. Volker Türk. He works for a very big group called the United Nations, or the UN for short.

Important Grown-Ups Are Watching

The United Nations is like a big team of grown-ups from almost all the countries in the world. Their job is to try and make sure everyone is treated fairly, that people live in peace, and that everyone is safe. Mr. Volker Türk's special job is to look after 'human rights.' That means he makes sure that every single person in the world, big or small, has the right to be safe, to be healthy, and to be treated with kindness. He heard about what is happening to the hospitals in Sudan, and he said it is very, very bad. He said these hurts to hospitals might be 'war crimes,' which means the people doing it are breaking those very important rules we just talked about. He is speaking up for all the doctors, nurses, and sick people in Sudan. **Did you know?** The United Nations was started many, many years ago to help countries talk to each other instead of fighting, and to help solve big problems around the world. They have a big blue flag with a world map on it! Even though this news can be a little sad, there is always hope! We can all hope for peace in Sudan. Peace means no more fighting, no more hurting hospitals, and everyone being kind to each other.

What Can We Do? Hope for Peace!

When there is peace, children can go to school, families can be together, and hospitals can help everyone get better without being scared. We can all send our best wishes and good thoughts to the children and families in Sudan. We can also be extra kind to our friends and family every day, because kindness is a superpower that can make the world a better place. You can help by sharing your toys, helping your parents, or saying nice words to your friends. Every little bit of kindness helps! We want all children, everywhere in Africa and the world, to be safe and happy. **Did you know?** Even a small act of kindness, like sharing a smile, can make a big difference in someone's day! Let's all be kindness champions! So, remember, hospitals are special, safe places. Hurting them is very wrong. Important people like Mr. Volker Türk are trying to help. And we, the children of Africa, can always hope for peace and be champions of kindness in our own homes and schools. Let's send our love to Sudan and hope for a brighter, safer tomorrow for everyone. This is Kiki the Reporter, signing off! Stay safe and keep shining, amazing kids!
summary: Some grown-ups fighting in Sudan are hurting hospitals on purpose, which is very wrong because hospitals are meant to be safe places for everyone, and important grown-ups like Mr. Volker Türk are saying this might be a 'war crime'.
whyMatters: This is important because hospitals help everyone get better, and when they are hurt, sick people, even children, cannot get the help they need, making life very scary and hard for many families in Sudan.
